frames.name: Setup
frames.finding: Safety core — MAIN and CHECKER cores in lockstep, comparator, fault latch, windowed watchdog, supply supervision.
lines: Safety core — MAIN and CHECKER cores in lockstep, comparator, fault latch, windowed watchdog, supply supervision.
Memory and boot — 64 KB mask ROM, 32 KB dual-port SRAM, QSPI flash controller.
Motor drive — 3-phase complementary PWM with dead-time and hardware brake, 4 × DShot, two timers.
Sensing and math — quadrature encoder and Hall decode, 8-bit differential SAR ADC, hardware CORDIC.
Connectivity — 2 × UART, SPI master, I²C master, GPIO.
Bus, system and test — two-master AXI-style bus with an error slave, 16-source interrupt controller, DMA, clock gating, JTAG and scan chains.

frames.name: Component flow
frames.finding: The PWM period centre fires the sample trigger.
lines: The PWM period centre fires the sample trigger.
The SAR ADC converts the phase current (177 cycles).
CORDIC runs the Clarke/Park transform with the rotor angle from the encoder (53–58 cycles per operation).
The CPU runs the d and q PI regulators in plain C (~8 cycles per instruction).
CORDIC runs the inverse Park rotation (53–58 cycles per operation).
Firmware writes the new duty cycles to the PWM shadow registers; they load at the next period boundary.
The lockstep comparator checks every committed store throughout; a mismatch latches and drives FAULT_N.

frames.name: Control / fault
frames.finding: A datapath fault changes a value MAIN commits.
lines: A datapath fault changes a value MAIN commits.
CHECKER, two cycles behind on identical inputs, commits a different value.
The comparator flags the mismatch on that store.
The fault CSR latches the first cause; FAULT_N goes low.
FAULT_N, routed to the gate-driver enable, turns the bridge off in hardware.

frames.name: Implication
frames.finding: Two cores and a comparator, not software self-test. A second core that must agree bit-for-bit catches datapath faults as they happen, in hardware, at a fixed latency. Software self-test runs periodically and cannot see a fault between runs.
lines: Two cores and a comparator, not software self-test. A second core that must agree bit-for-bit catches datapath faults as they happen, in hardware, at a fixed latency. Software self-test runs periodically and cannot see a fault between runs.

The loop runs in hardware. The CPU core is fetch-bound at ~8 cycles per instruction, so current sampling, the Park transforms and PWM edge generation are dedicated blocks and the CPU keeps only the PI regulators. That makes one loop's cost fixed and known.

Faults are contained, never silent. With no debugger halt on the die, every unmapped access returns a bus error, the watchdog catches both hangs and runaways, and the first fault cause is latched for later reading.

Flash-less die, boot from ROM. Loading the application from external QSPI flash into SRAM keeps the 130 nm process simple. The cost is boot-time loading instead of execute-in-place; embedded flash is on the roadmap.

frames.name: Setup
frames.finding: 50 MHz control domain — everything in DG32-LITE: lockstep CPU pair, fault latch and supervision, boot ROM and SRAM, motor drive, sensing and math, connectivity and test.
lines: 50 MHz control domain — everything in DG32-LITE: lockstep CPU pair, fault latch and supervision, boot ROM and SRAM, motor drive, sensing and math, connectivity and test.
114 MHz compute domain — the INT8 attention engine and its key/value buffers on SRAM macros.
Clock-domain bridges — three AXI bridges that carry programming and memory traffic between the two domains.

frames.name: Component flow
frames.finding: Firmware on the lockstep CPU writes the geometry through the lite bridge.
lines: Firmware on the lockstep CPU writes the geometry through the lite bridge.
Firmware sets start; the engine, on the 114 MHz clock, loads keys, values and the EXP table.
For each query row: multiply, weight, combine, requantise.
The engine writes the INT8 output back to memory through the burst write bridge.
The engine raises done; the interrupt controller delivers it to both cores.
A later kick can skip the load and reuse the resident keys, values and table.

frames.name: Control / fault
frames.finding: The PWM fires the ADC sample at the period centre.
lines: The PWM fires the ADC sample at the period centre.
CORDIC, the PI regulators and the PWM update run in the 50 MHz domain as on DG32-LITE.
The engine's traffic crosses only through the bridges, so it cannot extend the control core's worst-case execution time.

frames.name: Implication
frames.finding: A second clock, not an over-clocked die. The lockstep core tops out around 55–62 MHz, so the control domain stays at 50 MHz and the engine runs at 114 MHz behind bridges. The core's timing closure is never disturbed.
lines: A second clock, not an over-clocked die. The lockstep core tops out around 55–62 MHz, so the control domain stays at 50 MHz and the engine runs at 114 MHz behind bridges. The core's timing closure is never disturbed.

INT8 with unquantised weights, not INT4. With about 400 near-uniform keys, a 1/400 softmax weight rounds to zero in INT4 and the output came out identically zero. Keeping 15-bit weights all the way into a 40-bit numerator and saturating only the final output removes that failure structurally. A 32-bit numerator would break at 512 keys; 40 bits stays exact to 131,072.
Its own die. Adding the engine's memory macros to the DG32-LITE floorplan made routing time out. A bigger design gets a bigger die rather than a congested one.
Additions only. The frozen control core, boot path and bus decode are unchanged, so everything proven on DG32-LITE carries over.

frames.name: Setup
frames.finding: Host · control plane: A DGridRiscV core with timers and watchdog, SRAM and ReRAM, and the host interfaces. It sets the loop up and supervises it.
lines: Host · control plane: A DGridRiscV core with timers and watchdog, SRAM and ReRAM, and the host interfaces. It sets the loop up and supervises it.
Mixed signal: A 16-bit ADC for phase, bus and temperature, four reference DACs, an on-die temperature sensor and three current-sense amplifiers.
Power path: A buck-boost converter, seven PWM channels, three half-bridge pre-drivers, latched protection and runtime star or delta winding selection.
Field-oriented control datapath: A hardware PID tuner, a CORDIC rectangular-to-polar stage, inverse Park and Clarke, and sine or trapezoid lookup: torque command in, phase drive out.
Sensor + feedback: Hall, quadrature or encoder inputs give rotor angle and speed; the three phase currents are rebuilt, amplified and digitised.

frames.name: Setup
frames.finding: Input conditioning: EMI filter and TVS clamp, an ideal-diode reverse-polarity stage, soft-start inrush limiting, and hysteretic under- and over-voltage lockout.
lines: Input conditioning: EMI filter and TVS clamp, an ideal-diode reverse-polarity stage, soft-start inrush limiting, and hysteretic under- and over-voltage lockout.

Pre-regulator · synchronous buck: A type-III error amplifier, a PWM comparator with slope compensation, an adaptive dead-time gate driver, an LDMOS half-bridge power stage and sense-FET current sensing.
Reference + bias: A Brokaw bandgap at 1.20 V and 12 ppm/°C with one-time OTP trim, PTAT and CTAT bias, and an 8 MHz RC oscillator.

Rail generation: Four sequenced rails, two bucks at 5 V and 3.3 V and two LDOs at 1.8 V and 1.2 or 0.9 V, each followed by an over- and under-voltage window monitor and a foldback current limit that reports power-good.

Supervision · sequencing · telemetry: A programmable four-step sequencer, a 10-bit 500 kSPS telemetry ADC for voltage, current and die temperature over SPI, a windowed watchdog, and DICE latches with TMR on the sequencer state machine.

frames.finding: Sense chain · one per rail: For each of four rails: an ESD-protected input, a 0.1%-matched polysilicon divider, a chopper-stabilised comparator with 8 mV hysteresis, and an 8 µs digital deglitch counter.
lines: Sense chain · one per rail: For each of four rails: an ESD-protected input, a 0.1%-matched polysilicon divider, a chopper-stabilised comparator with 8 mV hysteresis, and an 8 µs digital deglitch counter.
Fault logic: A maskable, latched fault matrix with a priority encoder, mask register, latch and I²C registers.
Output stage: Open-drain FAULT_N, which asserts before RESET_N, an open-drain RESET_N with a trimmed 200 ms delay, and a manual-reset input.
Reference + timebase: A curvature-corrected bandgap at 1.20 V and 10 ppm/°C, a 5-bit OTP trim to ±0.5%, and an 8 MHz RC oscillator with a reference current.
Watchdog: A windowed watchdog adjustable from 100 ms to 1.6 s: an open and close window, a kick input, and a timeout counter that drives RESET_N.

frames.name: Component flow
frames.finding: ① Each rail enters through its divider.
lines: ① Each rail enters through its divider.
② The comparator and deglitch counter report a confirmed fault to the matrix.
③ The matrix latches it and drives FAULT_N, then RESET_N.
④ The trimmed bandgap sets every comparator threshold.
⑤ A missed or early watchdog kick times out to RESET_N.

frames.name: Control / fault
frames.finding: ② The comparator and deglitch counter report a confirmed fault to the matrix.
lines: ② The comparator and deglitch counter report a confirmed fault to the matrix.
③ The matrix latches it and drives FAULT_N, then RESET_N.

frames.name: Implication
frames.finding: Switching noise must not trip a reset, yet a real fault must still be caught quickly; the deglitch counter does both.
lines: Switching noise must not trip a reset, yet a real fault must still be caught quickly; the deglitch counter does both.
The bandgap and trimmed polysilicon resistors are what make the threshold accuracy possible on a mature node.

frames.finding: Chirp synthesis + transmit · SiGe die: A 40 MHz crystal, a ramp generator, a fractional-N PLL, a 38.5 GHz SiGe VCO and a doubler to 77 GHz, feeding two 13 dBm power amplifiers.
lines: Chirp synthesis + transmit · SiGe die: A 40 MHz crystal, a ramp generator, a fractional-N PLL, a 38.5 GHz SiGe VCO and a doubler to 77 GHz, feeding two 13 dBm power amplifiers.
Signal processing · CMOS die: A 1024-point radix-4 range FFT, a 128-point Doppler FFT across chirps, a range-Doppler map in 512 KB of SRAM, and windowing.
Receive array · 4 channels · SiGe die: Four identical channels: a 3.5 dB noise-figure LNA, a mixer fed by the LO, an IF amplifier, a 10 MHz anti-alias filter and a 12-bit 40 MSPS ADC.
Detection + output · CMOS die: Cell-averaging CFAR detection, digital-beamforming angle estimation at 15° resolution from four receivers, and a target list of up to 64 tracks per frame.

frames.name: Component flow
frames.finding: ① The crystal, ramp generator, PLL and VCO synthesise the chirp.
lines: ① The crystal, ramp generator, PLL and VCO synthesise the chirp.
② The doubler reaches 77 GHz and the two PAs transmit.
③ Each of four echoes is amplified, mixed with the LO, filtered and digitised.
④ The 12-bit samples cross to the CMOS die for the range FFT.
⑤ The range-Doppler map feeds CFAR detection and angle estimation.
⑥ The target list goes to the ECU over CAN-FD, 100BASE-T1 or MIPI CSI-2.

frames.finding: Video input: Four-lane LVDS and two-lane MIPI DSI receivers into a dual-port line buffer of four 1280-pixel, 24-bit lines.
lines: Video input: Four-lane LVDS and two-lane MIPI DSI receivers into a dual-port line buffer of four 1280-pixel, 24-bit lines.
Pixel pipeline: De-gamma, a 3 × 3 colour matrix with white point, a 14-bit gamma table with temperature feedback, and temporal and spatial dithering.
Timing + test: A timing controller with programmable porches, a 108 MHz pixel-clock PLL, a colour-bar test pattern and frame-freeze detection.

Column (source) drivers · high-voltage: One 10-bit resistor-string DAC per column and rail-to-rail high-voltage amplifiers swinging 0 to 12 V, driving 3,840 sub-pixel outputs with charge-sharing precharge.
Row + backlight: A gate-driver interface with a 24 V level shift, the VCOM electrode, an LED backlight with eight local-dimming zones, and ambient light and temperature sensing.

frames.name: Setup
frames.finding: Safety island: Two DGridRiscV cores in lockstep with a two-cycle skew, memory protection and ECC, a bus and retire comparator, and a freedom-from-interference firewall.
lines: Safety island: Two DGridRiscV cores in lockstep with a two-cycle skew, memory protection and ECC, a bus and retire comparator, and a freedom-from-interference firewall.
Security: A hardware security module with AES-256 and ECC-256, secure boot from an OTP key store with A/B slots, and an OTA engine with signed-image verification and rollback.
Real-time control: A TSN switch with an 802.1Qbv time-aware shaper, 802.1AS precision time, and a SOME/IP and DoIP service router.
In-vehicle network · gateway: The gateway ports: two 100BASE-T1, eight CAN-FD, one CAN-XL, eight LIN and one FlexRay. The gateway routes and rate-limits between domains.
Zonal power + I/O: Sixteen smart electronic fuses with sensing, eight high-side drivers, a 24-channel 12-bit sense ADC and twelve PWM actuator outputs.

lines: ① Messages arrive on Ethernet, CAN and LIN.
② The TSN switch schedules them against precision time.

④ They become switched power at the smart fuses.
⑤ A lockstep mismatch drives the safe state.

frames.name: Setup
frames.finding: Flight control: two DGridRiscV cores running the PX4 or ArduPilot loop, sensor and motor interfaces.
lines: Flight control: two DGridRiscV cores running the PX4 or ArduPilot loop, sensor and motor interfaces.
Visual-inertial odometry: camera input, image processing, feature extraction and a 30 Hz pose engine.
AI, variant 2 only: an INT8/INT4 NPU of about 10 TOPS on a 28 nm die.
Failsafe island: link monitor, safe-state machine and an independent path to the ESCs, on isolated power and clock.
Platform: memory, storage, power management, secure boot and external interfaces.

frames.name: Component flow
frames.finding: Sensors and the RC link reach the flight cores.
lines: Sensors and the RC link reach the flight cores.
The cameras run through the ISP and the feature extractor to the pose engine.
The 30 Hz pose reaches the flight loop over the crossbar.
The flight loop sends motor commands on ESC OUT.

frames.name: Control / fault
frames.finding: The link monitor sees RC loss, GPS loss or an IMU fault.
lines: The link monitor sees RC loss, GPS loss or an IMU fault.
It trips the safe-state FSM, which selects return to home or land.
The independent path takes the ESCs directly, bypassing the flight cores, odometry and AI.

frames.name: Implication
frames.finding: the sheet describes the odometry as geometry, not learned perception, so it needs no trained model to hold a pose.
lines: the sheet describes the odometry as geometry, not learned perception, so it needs no trained model to hold a pose.
vision AI needs dense logic that 130 nm cannot supply, so the accelerator is a 28 nm die that joins the same package in a later wave.
recovery must still work when the flight software is the thing that failed, so it cannot run as a task inside that software.
